To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the earnings distribution of the Spanish hotel industry is discontinuous, that is, a kink appears in the zero point.
there is a kink in both the earnings distribution (at the zero point) and the changes in earnings related with the previous year (at the zero and negative points) in the Spanish hotel sector.

the Spanish hotel industry shows a kink in earnings distribution and the incidence of certain characteristics (e.g. the number of rooms) in critical intervals of the earnings distribution is statistically significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of variables that determine the incidence of earnings management in the Spanish hotel sector.
identifying the variables that explain earnings management behaviour in the Spanish hotel sector.
the determinants of earnings benchmarks in the hotel industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Spanish hotel sector has a tendency to avoid earnings decreases and losses.

the variables that determine earnings management to avoid earnings decreases and losses in the hotel industry in Spain are: (i) the existence of a family ownership structure; (ii) the existence of an international chain; and (iii) the existence of the franchise system.

the variables that explain the incidence of small losses against small profits are different from those that explain the incidence in the other critical interval of the frequency distribution, small decreases in earnings versus small increases in earnings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Spanish hotel industry is characterised by the existence of a klink at the zero point in the frequency distribution of earnings, and that the critical interval is the small losses against small profits.
earnings benchmarks in the Spanish hotel sector are determined mainly by firm size, the level of debt, profitability, and the level of investment.

the variables that determine the avoidance of small earnings decreases and losses are different from those that determine the avoidance for small earnings increases and profits, and the avoidance of small losses and earnings decreases is determined by the same variables as the avoidance of small decreases in earnings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are significant differences in the determinants of earnings benchmarks between small and large companies, between companies with a higher and lower level of profitability, and between companies with a greater and lesser degree of financial leverage.
the incidence of the variables in the benchmark intervals is not the same for all firms.
the incidence of the variables is different in the critical intervals than in other intervals of the frequency histograms.
